flawed_step: 0039–0040: The assertion P − C = P is false. From Ac ≤ 0, one gets −Ac ≥ 0, so Ax − Ac need not be ≤ b.
counterexample: Let A=[-1] and b=0. Then P={x:-x≤0}=[0,∞), and its recession cone is C={c:-c≤0}=[0,∞). Choose x=0∈P and c=1∈C. Then x−c=−1∈P−C, but −1∉P because A(−1)=1>0=b. Indeed A(x−c)=1, contradicting line 0040's claimed inequality.
assessment_summary: The proof first definitively fails at lines 0039–0040 due to reversing the effect of subtracting a recession direction. Thus the proposed Step 2 construction is not justified.
